name: plan-queue
description: Track and run a plan's per-task prompts through Claude Code, one fresh context window per task.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Plan Queue runs Claude Code with file edits and an allowlist of shell commands on the prompts in a plan file, and runs shell commands from workspace settings. Trust the folder first.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Plan Queue needs a real folder to run Claude Code and git in.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No plans found.

Plan Queue looks for markdown files matching `$(gear) planQueue.planGlob` (default `docs/plans/**/*.md`) that contain a `## Prompts` section with one `### <id> — <title>` heading per task.

[Open settings](command:planQueue.openSettings)

commands.title: Run this task now, alongside the others
Open the prompt in the plan
Resume the task's session in a terminal
Allow the tools this task was denied
Open the plan's worktree in a new window
Discard the plan's worktree and branch

planQueue.planGlob.description: Workspace-relative glob for plan files. Only files with a '## Prompts' section are listed.

planQueue.claudePath.description: Path to the Claude Code CLI.

planQueue.model.description: Model passed to --model. Empty uses the CLI's default.

planQueue.permissionMode.description: --permission-mode each task's session starts with. acceptEdits auto-accepts file edits and runs the commands on planQueue.allowedTools; for anything else the session asks, and the task shows as waiting until you answer in its session.

enumDescriptions: Open a tab on each task's session as it starts, behind the tab you are looking at.
Open a task's tab only when it needs you (a question, or a prompt in its session) or has failed, behind the tab you are looking at. Click a task to open its session any time.
Never open one by itself; click a task, or use "Open the task's session".
planQueue.sessionTerminals.description: Each task runs as a Claude Code background session; its terminal runs `claude attach` on it, the full Claude Code UI. Closing the terminal leaves the session running.

enumDescriptions: An editor tab beside your files, as the Claude Code extension opens a session.
The terminal panel at the bottom.
planQueue.sessionTerminalLocation.description: Where a task's session terminal opens.

planQueue.allowedTools.description: Tools allowed without a prompt. Anything not listed is denied outright, so an unattended task fails loudly instead of waiting for an answer nobody will give.

planQueue.budgetUsd.description: Per-task ceiling passed to --max-budget-usd. 0 means no ceiling.
planQueue.budgetUsd.markdownDeprecationMessage: No longer applied: tasks run as interactive background sessions, and `--max-budget-usd` only works with `--print`.

planQueue.gateCommand.description: Shell command run after each task, in the task's working folder (the plan's worktree when it has one). A non-zero exit fails the task. Empty runs nothing.

planQueue.gateTimeoutMinutes.description: Kill the gate (and the worktree setup command) after this many minutes and count it as failed. 0 means no limit. Stop also kills a gate that is running.

planQueue.gateRetries.description: When the gate fails after a task said it was done, hand the gate's output back to the same session this many times to fix it before the task counts as blocked. 0 fails at once.

planQueue.resumeAfterLimit.description: When Claude Code hits the account's usage limit (5-hour or weekly), pause the running tasks instead of failing them, and carry on by itself once the limit resets. A plan started or resumed while the limit is on starts at the reset. Off leaves the paused tasks for you to resume by hand.

planQueue.limitResumeDelaySeconds.description: How long after the reset time the queue waits before it resumes, so the limit has really lifted.

planQueue.limitStartThreshold.description: Percent of a usage window (5-hour or weekly) at which the queue stops starting new tasks and waits for the reset, instead of running into the limit mid-task. 0 turns it off. Tasks already running carry on.
planQueue.limitStartThreshold.markdownDeprecationMessage: No longer applied: interactive sessions do not report how much of a usage window is used, so there is nothing to compare against. A task that hits the limit is still paused and resumed at the reset.

planQueue.resumeOnOpen.description: When the window opens, resume every plan that has a task paused by the window closing, in the same session. Tasks you paused by hand, and tasks paused by the usage limit (the limit timer handles those), are left alone.

planQueue.backlog.enabled.description: Start the plans on the backlog by itself, in order, when a run finishes, a usage limit lifts, the window opens, and every planQueue.backlog.sweepMinutes. An empty backlog does nothing.

planQueue.backlog.maxPlans.description: How many backlog plans may be running at once. A plan you started by hand counts if it is on the backlog.

planQueue.backlog.sweepMinutes.description: How often the backlog looks for a plan to start, in minutes, besides when a run finishes or a usage limit lifts. 0 turns the interval off.

planQueue.transientRetries.description: When a task's turn is cut off by a temporary API error (overloaded, 5xx, a dropped connection), wait 1 minute, then 5, and carry on in the same session, this many times before the task counts as blocked. 0 fails at once.

planQueue.stopOnFailure.description: Halt the queue when a task is blocked or its gate fails.

planQueue.stashFailedWork.description: When a task in a plan's worktree is blocked, fails its gate or is stopped, stash what it left in the tree (git stash, untracked files included) so the next task and the next commit start from what passed. The log names the stash. Off leaves the changes in the tree, where the next passing task's commit picks them up.

planQueue.requireSentinel.description: Treat a task as done only when it ends with PLAN_QUEUE: DONE. A turn that ends with no sentinel is asked once whether it is done, blocked or asking something. With this off, exit code 0 is enough.

planQueue.useAgentFromPlan.description: Pass the agent named in a task heading to --agent when this install has it. When it does not, the role is named in the prompt instead.

planQueue.extraArgs.description: Extra arguments for the `claude --bg` command that starts each task's session. A resumed session keeps the options it started with.

planQueue.logThinking.description: Include the model's thinking in the log. Off, the log shows what it says and the tools it calls.

planQueue.worktrees.description: Run each plan on a branch of its own in a git worktree of its own, so several plans can run at once. Each passing task is committed there; when every task is done or skipped the branch is merged into the branch it was cut from. Required in a git repository: Claude Code background sessions isolate their edits in a worktree, so a task run in place would not change the workspace. Outside a git repository, plans run in the workspace one at a time.

planQueue.worktreeRoot.description: Folder the plan worktrees are created in, absolute or relative to the repository root. Empty uses <repo>/.claude/worktrees (kept out of git status through .git/info/exclude). Keep it under a .claude/worktrees folder: anywhere else, Claude Code moves each task's edits into a worktree of its own.

planQueue.worktreeSetupCommand.description: Shell command run once in a new worktree before its first task, e.g. `npm ci`. A worktree starts with only what is committed, so dependencies and build output have to be recreated. Empty runs nothing.

planQueue.mergeWhenDone.description: Merge a plan's branch into its base branch (with --no-ff) once every task is done or skipped, then remove the worktree. A conflict aborts the merge and keeps the branch. Off leaves the branch for you to merge or open a PR from.

planQueue.startPlansAfterMerge.description: When a plan's branch merges, start every plan whose `Runs after:` line names it, once all the plans that line names are finished. The next plan's worktree is cut from the branch that now holds the merge. Needs worktrees and mergeWhenDone.

planQueue.maxParallelTasks.description: How many tasks of one plan may work at the same moment. Only tasks that declare `Depends on:` ever run side by side; a plan without those lines runs one task at a time whatever this is. They share the plan's one working tree, so give parallel tasks disjoint files. A task waiting for your reply does not count.

planQueue.server.enabled.description: Serve a local MCP and command-line endpoint (127.0.0.1, bearer-token protected) so Claude Code, or the `pq` command, can list, start, watch, answer and stop plans. Use the command 'Plan Queue: Connect Claude Code' to turn it on and register it.

planQueue.server.port.description: Port for the control endpoint. With several VS Code windows open, only the first to start gets it.

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build
scripts.package: npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build && npx --yes @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies -o plan-queue.vsix
scripts.test: node --test test/parse.test.mjs test/git.test.mjs test/verdict.test.mjs test/schedule.test.mjs test/describe.test.mjs test/chain.test.mjs test/limits.test.mjs test/backlog.test.mjs test/session.test.mjs
scripts.pretest: npx esbuild src/plan.ts src/git.ts src/verdict.ts src/schedule.ts src/describe.ts src/chain.ts src/limits.ts src/backlog.ts src/session.ts --bundle --platform=node --format=esm --outdir=out --out-extension:.js=.mjs --log-level=error
